Treatment summary
Patient presented following a collision sustained while turning left, when the vehicle was struck by another car. The reported
mechanism is consistent with the shoulder injury diagnosed, and the force involved would be expected to produce this type of
soft tissue damage. Over the course of 17 visits, care included physical therapy, range of motion work, and home exercise
instruction. The duration of treatment was somewhat longer than typically seen for a shoulder injury of this kind, and progress
was gradual. On examination, several findings support the presence of a shoulder injury, including reduced range of motion and
tenderness over the affected area, while other tests, including neurovascular checks and certain stability assessments, were within
normal limits. No prior injury to the same shoulder has been reported or identified in the patient's history. Billing records for this
episode of care are currenlty under routine review, as two similar charges appearing on the same day are being verified. Ongoing
reassessment is planned to monitor function and guide the remaining plan of care.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),

  spelling errors as they are,
